caption:
Replit CEO Amjad Masad said onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt that Replit no longer works with Anthropic.
He cited cost, partnership and performance, and said OpenAI's models now win on Replit's benchmarks.
A person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch the partnership is still in place.

Is this a real breakup or just a negotiation tactic?

slides.headline: Replit's CEO says it dumped Anthropic because *OpenAI is better now*

slides.heading: A yes *onstage*
paras: Asked at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday whether Replit's OpenAI deal meant it no longer worked with Anthropic, CEO Amjad Masad answered yes.
He said the choice came down to cost, partnership and performance, and called OpenAI the better partner "for now."

slides.heading: The *benchmark* argument
paras: Masad said Replit's internal benchmark and a public one both show OpenAI's Sol and Astra models building vibe-coded apps from scratch better.
Replit announced its OpenAI partnership in August, when it launched a Free Mode powered by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna.

slides.heading: Not so *fast*
paras: A person familiar with the partnership told TechCrunch it is still in place. A Replit blog post in September listed Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 running in production.

paras.t: Replit's own model list still shows several Claude models next to OpenAI's. TechCrunch asked Replit to clarify.

slides.heading: Replit's *business* shift
paras: Masad said enterprise contracts are about 15% of Replit's revenue this year, up from about 2% last year.
More than half of its revenue now comes from businesses, he said. He declined to share annual recurring revenue.

slides.hook: The AI model war just claimed a big customer. Follow so you catch the next switch first.
